title: A fireball over northern China on 6 November 2026 punched a crater into a wheat field at Beigucheng village in Hebei; the Institute of Geochemistry has now classified the fallen stones as L6 ordinary chondrites.
excerpt: More than 200 kg (440 pounds) of meteorites has been recovered near Shijiazhuang in China’s Hebei province after the November 6, 2026 fireball, according to an estimate from an observatory engineer.
content:
More than 200 kg (440 pounds) of meteorites has been recovered near Shijiazhuang in China’s Hebei province after the November 6, 2026 fireball, according to an estimate from an observatory engineer. The recovered rocks have been provisionally classified as L6 ordinary chondrites. The designation points to heating inside their parent body long before they reached Earth.

The estimate came from Xu Zhijian, an engineer at the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Purple Mountain Observatory, in a November 15 report by China Central Television (CCTV). It covered the combined recovery; the largest intact individual stone mentioned in the report weighed 35 kg (77 pounds).

The fireball crossed northern China at about 10:31 UTC on November 6 (18:31 China Standard Time), with sightings in Beijing, Hebei and Shanxi. Surveillance footage supplied by the Yangquan Astronomy Society in Shanxi shows the flash illuminating the evening sky.

Residents and meteorite hunters subsequently recovered fragments from farmland around Shijiazhuang. Local reporting placed one recovery site in a wheat field at Beigucheng village, in the city’s Luquan district.

Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences’ Institute of Geochemistry examined recovered samples using scanning electron microscopy to study their internal structures and mineral composition. The samples were provisionally identified as L6 ordinary chondrites, a common type of stony meteorite, in results reported on November 10.

The L places the samples in the low-iron group of ordinary chondrites. The 6 describes strong heating on their parent body, where minerals recrystallized, and many original grain outlines became indistinct. This structure records conditions inside the parent body long before the November 6 atmospheric entry.

Those rounded grains, known as chondrules, are an important part of how chondrites are classified. The Meteoritical Bulletin Database defines type 6 as material in which metamorphism has erased many chondrule outlines without melting the rock.

“Meteorites collected immediately after falling are generally very fresh,” Li Shijie, a researcher at the institute, told The Beijing News (translated from Chinese). He said their limited exposure to terrestrial material makes them useful for studying their original composition.

The fall also provides a chance to connect the stones with observations of the object that delivered them. Li explained that reconstructing a meteorite’s approach can help researchers investigate the orbits of small bodies and improve understanding of potential impacts.

According to the institute’s account reported by The Beijing News, additional footage from multiple locations, with reliable times and viewing directions, could help refine the flight path and the area where fragments landed. Combined with the recovered samples, that information could help researchers investigate the object’s possible source.

References

1 CCTV News, republished by China Youth Network. “落地陨石价值几何？新鲜度、类型才是科学标尺” [What determines a fallen meteorite’s value? Freshness and type are scientific criteria]. November 15, 2026. In Chinese.

2 Xinhua. “山西阳泉上空现‘火流星’ 清华团队动画还原其轨道” [Fireball appears over Yangquan, Shanxi; Tsinghua team animates its orbit]. November 7, 2026. In Chinese.

3 Global Times. “Chinese researchers preliminarily classify meteorite fragments found in N.China’s Hebei as L6 ordinary chondrites”. November 10, 2026. Reporting the Institute of Geochemistry’s announcement.

4 Wang Jingxi, The Beijing News. “华北‘火流星’初步判定为普通球粒陨石，研究价值高吗？” [Northern China fireball samples provisionally identified as ordinary chondrites: what is their research value?]. November 10, 2026. In Chinese.

5 Meteoritical Bulletin Database. Recommended classifications: L6. Definitions of the L group and petrologic type
